udb 0.5.8 — proto-driven multi-database broker

USAGE:
  udb <command> [args] [flags]
  udb help <command>      show a command's flags + example
  udb <command> --help    same
  udb --version

COMMANDS:

  Core:
    serve                  Start the broker (syncs schema from protos; control plane on data-port+10).
    requirements           Print the backend contract this project's manifest declares (run before first start).
    doctor                 Env + backend readiness; --enterprise adds a manifest-aware prerequisite preflight.

  Schema & SQL:
    lint                   Lint the catalog built from your annotated protos (CI-safe; nonzero on errors).
    drift                  Diff the manifest against a prior one; flags destructive/blocked changes.
    sql                    Emit the generated bootstrap SQL artifacts as JSON (no DB touched).
    plan                   Build a migration plan (optionally vs a prior manifest) as JSON.
    catalog                Dump the parsed proto catalog as JSON.
    dsn                    Print the unified DSN catalog derived from the protos.
    manifest-export        Export the current CatalogManifest to JSON (for CI plan-approval).

  Auth & policy:
    auth migrate-grants    Migrate legacy profile-attribute service grants into the typed service_account_grants table.
    auth bootstrap user    Mint the FIRST admin OFFLINE (no running broker needed); prints the canonical tenant UUID.
    auth api-key create    Mint an API key (tenant-scoped).
    auth api-key list/revoke List an owner's API keys or revoke one OFFLINE (UDB-AUTH-009 rotation/reconciliation).
    auth grant             Manage typed service-account grants through the authenticated native API.
    auth cert-binding      Manage mTLS certificate bindings through the authenticated native API.
    auth policy put        Write a control-plane Casbin governance rule (NOT the data-plane ABAC gate).
    policy-lint            Lint ABAC policy files from UDB_ABAC_POLICY_FILE (nonzero on broken files).
    policy-seed

udb auth migrate-grants — Migrate legacy profile-attribute service grants into the typed service_account_grants table.

USAGE:
  udb auth migrate-grants [--dry-run]

Needs UDB_PG_DSN. Deterministic: scans ACTIVE service accounts, validates each
  profile grant (admin/wildcard scopes and duplicate identities are REJECTED and
  reported, never partially written), and creates one typed grant per account.
  --dry-run reports without writing. After migration the typed grant is the
  authoritative source for password login, API keys, and mTLS bindings.

udb auth cert-binding — Manage mTLS certificate bindings through the authenticated native API.

USAGE:
  udb auth cert-binding <create|list|revoke> --tenant <tenant-id> [flags]

Needs UDB_AUTH_TARGET (or UDB_GRPC_TARGET) and UDB_AUTH_TOKEN.
  create: --tenant <tenant-id> --user <uuid> --selector-kind <k> --selector-value <v>
          [--scope <s>…] [--not-before-unix <seconds>] [--not-after-unix <seconds>]
          [--reason <r>]
  list:   --tenant <tenant-id>
  revoke: --tenant <tenant-id> --binding <id> [--reason <r>]
  Selector kinds: SPIFFE_URI, DNS_SAN, SUBJECT_CN, FINGERPRINT_SHA256. The
  account must hold an ACTIVE grant; --scope attenuates it (empty = full grant).
  Re-creating a REVOKED selector supersedes the old row in place (same id).

udb authz seed — Seed the STANDARD data-plane authorization for a project (idempotent, offline).

USAGE:
  udb authz seed --tenant <uuid> [--role app_rw] [--entity <fqn> …] [--action <verb> …] [--project <id>] [--dsn <dsn>] [--emit <path>]

The straightforward way to stop fighting `PERMISSION_DENIED` on CRUD. Writes one
  role-gated ALLOW policy per (entity, action) into `udb_authz.policy_rules` — the
  table the data plane actually enforces — using the REAL action tokens the broker
  submits (`Select`/`Upsert`/`Delete`/`Update`/`BulkCas`, NOT a `data.*` alias) and
  the canonical tenant UUID. Postgres-direct (needs UDB_PG_DSN/DATABASE_URL or
  --dsn); run it right after `udb auth bootstrap user`. Idempotent (safe to re-run)
  and atomic (all rows in one tx, so an open `UDB_ABAC_DEFAULT_ALLOW` window never
  half-closes).
Defaults: `--role app_rw`, all data actions, object `*` (the whole catalog).
  `--entity <fqn>` (repeatable) narrows to specific message types; `--action <verb>`
  (repeatable) narrows the verbs; `--emit <path>` also writes the equivalent
  offline policy JSON for version control.
Then bind principals (users AND service accounts) to the role so the policy
  applies: `udb auth role bind --principal <id> --role <role> --tenant <uuid>`.
Example: udb authz seed --tenant 00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000d0001 --role app_rw
